Hi all — hi Olivia, good to meet you over email. Below is a concise matrix of feasible export patterns and how they map to your asks. I attached a short PDF with formats and a sample signed manifest.

Option A — Streaming: Pub/Sub (GCP) or Kafka (customer-managed)
- Delivery: per-event push; we guarantee max 45s median fanout in our hosted regions (SLA via Dedicated contracts).
- Integrity: HMAC-signed hourly manifest alongside per-event sequence numbers. We also provide a signed checkpoint file every hour.
- Redaction: deterministic SHA-256 hashing (configurable salt) for identity fields so you can reconcile across days without PII exposure.
- Legal hold: we can switch stream to "preserve-only" mode (events continue, but a copy is appended to an immutable archive bucket where TTL is suspended).

Option B — Hourly micro-batch (NDJSON or Parquet)
- Delivery: hourly bundle (gzip) to S3/GCS with signed manifest and checksum.
- Redaction: configurable field-level redaction rules (keep hashed_user_id, redact email/ip) defined via redaction_field_map.csv.
- Retention: per-bucket lifecycle rules; we can map retention windows to roles via manifest metadata.

Option C — Snapshot attested bundle (for audits)
- Delivery: on-demand snapshot with chain-of-custody manifest, PGP-signed and timestamped. Good for formal evidence handoff.

Notes on format & sampling:
- Auditors typically accept Parquet for large volumes; NDJSON is easier for quick inspection.
- We can include an example signed_manifest_example.txt that shows HMAC header, start/end times, number of events, SHA-256 checksum, and creator signature.

Timeline for sample (T+24): if you want the streaming sample, we can enable a dedicated export hook and deliver a signed 24-hour snapshot within 48 hours of agreement (we need a short SOW). For an hourly NDJSON sample we can deliver within 24 hours.

Attachments included: audit_feed_options_v1.pdf, signed_manifest_example.txt, redaction_field_map.csv
